code_actions.rationale: No documentation in progress notes or discharge diagnoses explicitly supports a diagnosis of anoxic brain damage; cognitive impairment is attributed to HSV encephalitis in the chart, so G93.1 is unsupported and removed.
The chart documents new post-encephalitis cognitive impairment and memory problems but does not document pre-existing dementia with behavioral disturbance; remove F02.81 as unsupported.
Vascular dementia is not supported by the chart (H&P documents previously healthy, and discharge attributes cognitive impairment to encephalitis); remove.

Chart documents a catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT but does not explicitly document an insertion procedure of an infusion device into the superior vena cava; insufficient specific documentation to support this exact PCS (remove unless operative/procedure note supports).

evidence.quote: Principal Diagnosis Refractory status epilepticus; HSV-1 encephalitis
The patient was intubated for airway protection with escalation of anticonvulsants and empiric acyclovir initiation given clinical suspicion for HSV encephalitis.
CSF HSV-1 PCR was positive and MRI demonstrated bilateral temporal lobe changes characteristic of HSV encephalitis; a full 21-day course of intravenous acyclovir was completed.
New-onset refractory status epilepticus secondary to HSV encephalitis
Interval: sputum culture growing Streptococcus pneumoniae; narrowing antibiotics; continuing HSV encephalitis treatment NAEON; cont current Rx 2/2 critical illness.
prolonged mechanical ventilation requiring tracheostomy on ICU day 14, PEG placement for enteral nutrition on ICU day 16, and profound ICU-acquired weakness.
catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation
ABG (02:00): pH 7.28 / PaCO2 45 / PaO2 66 / HCO3 18; lactate 5.2 mmol/L; P/F ratio 73.

Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses Resolved refractory status epilepticus; treated HSV-1 encephalitis; ongoing cognitive impairment from encephalitis; residual right-sided weakness; resolved aspiration pneumonia (S. pneumoniae); tracheostomy-dependent respiratory status (trach collar); catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT on anticoagulation; resolved SIADH; ICU-acquired weakness.

system_note: This DRG review examined all billed diagnoses and procedures against the chart. Summary of key findings and supporting documentation: 1) Principal diagnosis sequencing: the medical record consistently documents refractory status epilepticus as the condition that occasioned admission and HSV-1 encephalitis as the underlying cause (supporting sequencing status epilepticus as principal). See ev_0004 (Discharge/Transfer Summary: Admission Diagnoses: New-onset refractory status epilepticus secondary to HSV encephalitis) and ev_0001 (H&P: Principal Diagnosis Refractory status epilepticus; HSV-1 encephalitis). Nothing in the record contradicts B00.4 independently, so B00.4 (Herpesviral encephalitis) is kept as the principal diagnosis and G41.0 is retained as a secondary diagnosis (evidence: ev_0004, ev_0001). 2) HSV-1 encephalitis is well-supported and present on admission: CSF HSV-1 PCR positive and MRI with bilateral temporal lobe changes; empiric acyclovir was started on presentation (evidence: ev_0003, ev_0002). Keep B00.4 as principal; POA=Y. 3) Several billed secondary diagnoses are supported by the record and should be retained (acute respiratory failure, coma, aspiration pneumonia with Streptococcus pneumoniae, SIADH, catheter-associated right IJ DVT, anterograde amnesia, right-sided hemiparesis/hemiplegia, ventilator dependence): evidence includes admission/ICU notes, microbiology and progress notes, and the discharge/transfer summary (evidence: ev_0009 for respiratory failure ABG/P/F values; ev_0005 and for S. pneumoniae aspiration pneumonia; ev_0008 for catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT; ev_0006 for tracheostomy and PEG). 4) Diagnoses without adequate chart support (remove): G93.1 (anoxic brain damage) — the chart and the discharge diagnoses attribute the cognitive deficits to HSV encephalitis and post-encephalitis impairment rather than a documented anoxic brain injury; there is no progress note or discharge problem explicitly diagnosing anoxic brain damage (evidence: ev_0010 [the discharge diagnoses list shows post-encephalitis cognitive impairment and does not list anoxic brain damage] and ev_0003/ev_0004 showing HSV encephalitis as the explanatory cause). 5) Duplicate / unsupported dementia codes: both F02.81 (dementia in other diseases with behavioral disturbance) and F03.B0 (vascular dementia) are billed; the record documents new post-encephalitis cognitive impairment and memory impairment but documents the patient as previously healthy with no prior dementia (H&P). There is no documentation supporting pre-existing vascular dementia (remove F02.81 and F03.B0) (evidence: ev_0001 and ev_0010). 6) Procedure-level unsupported PCS: the billed PCS 02HV33Z is not supported by specific documentation — the chart documents a catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT but does not explicitly document an insertion procedure of an infusion device into the superior vena cava; insufficient specific documentation to support this exact PCS (remove unless an operative/procedure note supports it) (evidence: ev_0008). 7) Procedure-level conflict (human review required): billed tracheostomy code is 0B110F4 (open tracheostomy). The H&P problem list explicitly records “Percutaneous tracheostomy for prolonged coma” while the chart elsewhere documents that a tracheostomy was performed on ICU day 14 but does not clearly state approach. This is a direct conflict between the clinical documentation lines and the billed PCS approach (see ). Because the approach (percutaneous vs open) determines the correct ICD-10-PCS code, this requires human adjudication before retaining 0B110F4 or substituting the appropriate percutaneous tracheostomy code (evidence: ev_0007 and ev_0006). 8) Other procedures (endotracheal intubation on admission, LP, PEG, EEG monitoring, prolonged ventilation >96 hours) are documented and supported (evidence: ev_0002, ev_0003, ev_0006). Correction summary (claim-level): - Keep principal diagnosis B00.4 (Herpesviral encephalitis) — role principal; POA=Y; severity=MCC. - Retain G41.0 (Grand mal status epilepticus) as a secondary diagnosis; POA=Y; severity=MCC. - Remove G93.1 (anoxic brain damage) — unsupported in the record. - Remove F02.81 and F03.B0 (dementia codes) — unsupported / contradicted by admission H&P and discharge summary which attribute cognitive deficits to encephalitis, not pre-existing dementia. - Remove PCS 02HV33Z (unsupported insertion procedure documentation). - Retain acute respiratory failure (J96.01), unspecified coma (R40.9), aspiration pneumonia (J69.0) and pneumonia due to S. pneumoniae (J13), SIADH (E22.2), catheter-associated right IJ DVT (I82.C11), anterograde amnesia (R41.1), right hemiplegia (G81.94), Z99.11 ventilator dependence, and procedures for intubation, LP, PEG, EEG monitoring, and prolonged ventilation >96 hours. - Remove billed open tracheostomy 0B110F4 pending clinician confirmation of surgical approach (open vs percutaneous); if percutaneous approach is confirmed, the PCS should be recoded accordingly. Evidence relied on (document/section/page are provided from the citations below): ev_0001, ev_0002, ev_0003, ev_0004, ev_0005, ev_0006, ev_0007, ev_0008, ev_0009. Because the tracheostomy approach is unresolved in the record this review is a Finding and requires human escalation to confirm PCS approach before final procedure-list coding. Detailed evidence citations are in evidence_cited.
rationale_letter:
To: Medical Records/Coding Department
Re: MR_16 — DRG-level audit determination
We performed a full DRG-level audit of the above inpatient stay, comparing the billed diagnosis and procedure set to the medical record documentation. Findings: After review of the chart (H&P, progress notes, consult notes, and discharge/transfer summary), we find that several secondary diagnoses require correction, the principal diagnosis sequencing (B00.4 versus G41.0) is a question for reviewer confirmation with the billed principal B00.4 retained, and one procedure requires clinician clarification before the hospital may substantiate its PCS coding. Basis for determination (selected chart evidence): - The chart documents “New-onset refractory status epilepticus secondary to HSV encephalitis” and the H&P lists the principal diagnosis as refractory status epilepticus with HSV-1 encephalitis (see Discharge/Transfer Summary Admission Diagnoses and H&P, ev_0004 and ev_0001). Nothing in the record contradicts B00.4 independently, so B00.4 (Herpesviral encephalitis) is kept as the principal diagnosis and G41.0 is retained as a secondary diagnosis. - HSV-1 encephalitis is confirmed in the record: CSF HSV-1 PCR positive and MRI with bilateral temporal lobe changes; a full intravenous acyclovir course was completed (see ev_0003). Keep B00.4 as principal, POA=Y. - Aspiration pneumonia with Streptococcus pneumoniae is documented in progress and consult notes (sputum culture growing S. pneumoniae, targeted antibiotics), supporting J69.0 and J13 as secondary diagnoses (see ev_0005). - Tracheostomy and PEG placement are documented; prolonged mechanical ventilation is documented and supports the >96-hour ventilation procedure code (see ev_0006). - The record does not contain authoritative documentation of anoxic brain damage (G93.1). The discharge diagnoses attribute cognitive deficits to HSV encephalitis / post-encephalitis impairment rather than an anoxic brain injury; no note explicitly diagnoses anoxic brain damage. Therefore G93.1 is unsupported and will be removed. - Two billed dementia codes (F02.81 and F03.B0) are not supported by the chart: the patient is documented as previously healthy with new cognitive impairment related to encephalitis, not pre-existing vascular dementia or established dementia; those codes will be removed. - The billed ICD-10-PCS for tracheostomy (0B110F4 — open tracheostomy) conflicts with a contemporaneous clinical line that documents “Percutaneous tracheostomy for prolonged coma” (H&P problem list). Because PCS approach (open vs percutaneous) materially changes the correct code, we require clinician clarification. Action taken: - Principal diagnosis retained as B00.4 (Herpesviral encephalitis) — principal, POA=Y, severity=MCC. - G41.0 (Grand mal status epilepticus) retained as a secondary diagnosis — POA=Y, severity=MCC. - Removed diagnoses: G93.1 (anoxic brain damage), F02.81 (dementia in other diseases w/ behavioral disturbance), F03.B0 (vascular dementia). - Removed procedure/PCS: 02HV33Z (unsupported specific documentation of the insertion procedure described by this PCS). - Retained secondary diagnoses supported by the chart: R40.9, J96.01, J69.0, J13, E22.2, I82.C11, R41.1, G81.94, Z99.11. - Procedures retained: endotracheal intubation, lumbar puncture, PEG, EEG monitoring, prolonged mechanical ventilation (>96 hours). - Procedure 0B110F4 (open tracheostomy) removed pending clinician clarification of percutaneous vs open approach; recoding to the correct PCS will be completed on receipt of clarification. Please provide written clarification (operative report or procedural note) stating the tracheostomy approach (open vs percutaneous) and the date the procedure was performed. If an operative/procedure note confirms an open tracheostomy, we will reinstate 0B110F4; if percutaneous, we will substitute the appropriate PCS code. Thank you. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Auditor
